<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Turning the knob back and forth quickly backs up requests: every click is its own job doing a fresh-connection /Volume read and a write (2 s timeouts), handled one at a time, so bursts queue and stale clicks get dropped. Coalesce all pending clicks into one net volume change per round, keep the HTTP connection to the amp alive, and only redraw the screen when nothing is queued or in flight (the screen is for debugging, and full redraws run on the loop that receives the knob). The safety basis is unchanged: a fresh read before each write, increases written as an absolute level checked against max_db; a burst past the cap stops at max_db.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- Fast back-and-forth turning feels immediate: one amp round-trip per burst, not per click.
- No safety regression: never past max_db; fresh read before each write; unchanged mute/source behaviour.
- Screen redraws never compete with knob handling or amp requests.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Dropping the fresh /Volume read (safety basis).
- Changing mute/source commands beyond queue ordering.
- New screen designs.

<a id="key-findings"></a>

## Key Findings

| impact | finding | action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| High | Per-click read+write with a new connection each time is the backlog source. | Coalesce + keep-alive. |
| High | Full-screen redraws run on loop(), which also drains the BLE queue. | Redraw only when idle. |
| Critical | Plan 002 safety rules (fresh read, abs increases, muted basis) are the cap's basis. | Keep them; clamp combined increases to max_db. |
